previous_description: An aggregate container defining the procedural access control constraints for an application, grouping SeparationOfDuty, BindingOfDuty, and NeedToKnow rules. Applied within SecurityModel to enforce AC-5 and workflow integrity controls.
definition: An application-scoped container that groups the procedural, workflow-level access constraints (SeparationOfDuty, BindingOfDuty and NeedToKnow rules) applied within a SecurityModel. It holds no predicate or decision logic of its own; its content is the set of duty and purpose constraints it aggregates.

distinguish_from.when: modelling one specific rule that two tasks or roles must be held by different actors, rather than the collection of all such rules for the application
the artifact is a prioritized set of evaluable rules with permit/deny effects targeting endpoints, data or roles, rather than a grouping of duty and need-to-know constraints
the element is the root security specification for the application, composing authentication, roles, threats, classification and policies, not only the procedural constraints
modelling a single purpose-justification requirement for one resource rather than the grouping container

standard_reference: NIST SP 800-53 AC-5 (Separation of Duties), with AC-3(3) need-to-know restrictions
code_evidence: a dedicated configuration block or file (e.g. 'constraints:' or 'duty-rules.yaml') listing separation-of-duty pairs, binding-of-duty tasks and need-to-know resources together
a registry or module (e.g. WorkflowConstraintRegistry, DutyConstraintService) that loads and applies several SoD/BoD/purpose checks to workflow transitions such as request/approve
a documentation section titled e.g. 'Procedural Access Constraints' or 'Segregation of Duties Matrix' enumerating mutually exclusive roles and task-continuity rules for one application

attribute_descriptions.name: version
attribute_descriptions.description: Version identifier of this constraint set (e.g. semantic version '1.2.0' or a dated revision), set when the grouped duty and need-to-know rules are versioned independently of the enclosing SecurityModel.

notes: Container has no scoping attribute (application/scope) and no description; consider adding them. Outgoing 'enforces' and 'governs' to securitypolicy are redundant and odd for a passive container. Incoming 'satisfies' from apm.logprocessor, navigationflow and objectschema target the container rather than individual rules, which weakens traceability; consider redirecting to the aggregated rule types.
